analysis:
The only change in this PR is one line of documentation in docs/developer/test.md (base/head line 494). It adds `RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark` to the `swift test --skip-build --filter` regex for the focused runtime-generation policy and CLI checks. No runtime code, protocol, key handling, cache-storage logic, authorization path, workflow or release script is touched.

I checked the surrounding unchanged text in all three units for security-relevant guidance that the edit could weaken. The nearby text keeps prefix caches off for runtime generation, requires an owned GPU and a verified model, and states that these are not checkpoint-storage comparisons. The broader document keeps isolated state, production cache roots and keys excluded, and skips and failures reported honestly. This matches the T-041 cache posture: encrypted SSD, HMAC lookup tags and the 30-minute TTL are unaffected.

The added filter token only widens which tests the local `swift test` invocation selects. It introduces no new environment variable, credential, network target or privileged operation. A possible hazard is that a new test selected by the filter could touch real provider state or caches. That would depend on the test source, which is not supplied. The doc keeps the isolation and no-production-state instructions, and I found no evidence of a regression.

No threat-model entries are invalidated and no model update is needed. The remaining integration question is whether a `RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark` suite exists and respects the isolated-state conventions in scripts/run-provider-tests.sh. That is outside the supplied evidence and does not support a finding.
